Interesting observations! Well, now, on the reread of New Spring, I think chapter 13 or 14, Moiraine and Siuan briefly consider bringing Sheriam into their circle of trust, but decide not to because Sheriam was one of the worst pladderers and rumour spreaders of their Accepted time. I personally consider this possible proof for her Darkfriend status at this time already; it was obviously a disguise. If not, it was something that changed rapidly once she joined the ranks of the Aes Sedai; no one becomes Black Ajah and talks widely about things. I'm not sure. It's definitely possible that she was a Darkfriend already, hiding her true intentions behind seemingly foolishly spreading rumours. But yeah... I also liked Sheriam, ever until her true allegiance was revealed. I for one found it absolutely detestable by Sanderson to reveal it before Egwene could find it in Verin's list herself. Imagine the shock both for Egwene and us, something along these lines:

"Swiftly eyeing once through the list to see its reach, one name drew Egwene's eyes to itself, as surely as iron pulled to a magnet, with a sweeping, sinking surge of arising panic. Like all of Verin's notations, it was written in a short and efficient manner. ''Sheriam Bayanar. Almost certainly on the Black Ajah Supreme Council." The shock hit Egwene like a punch to the stomach. ''Sheriam. Sheriam is Black Ajah.'' Warm, caring Sheriam, although a devious politician, a woman of warmth. Black Ajah."

As for Danelle, such a "dreamy, introvert" sister taking such a rapid and bold decision? Instantly put her under suspicion. Verin never truly struck me as Black, which she, in the end, also never truly was. To the very last line, I was convinced she was a champion for the Light, albeit with very controversial and different methods.

Lelaine and Romanda! An interesting notation. Lelaine, like many Blues, is a bit too dogged in having things her way, easily leading to suspicion, and truly, once she assumed command of Siuan, Leane and the others around Egwene and  practically of the Salidar Six by ''Knife of Dreams'', I can imagine the possibility. Romanda, however? No, never. She always struck me as a stoic, somewhat too set in tradition, fighting force for good.
